Hooked
When the story
writes us
EMOTIONAL
2 | PERCY POF-ENG HSU E
04-0061

A Hollywood script lives or dies by its
"hook": the simple premise that captures
the audience's interest, sets the story in
motion, and drives the action forward.
We may not take meetings with movie stars,
but each of us, in our own way, is a
screenwriter. Every minute of every day,
we're writing the scripts that get screened
at the cinema inside our heads.
But in our own stories, getting hooked isn't
an edge-of-your-seat thrill. It's self-defeating
reactivity:
"There's no point in trying."
"That's the way we've always done it."
"No one ever listens anyway."
EMOTIONAL
02026 SUSAN DAVID V2 1 PERCY POF-ENG HSU EAC-C04-0061

Teams and cultures feel it too. Silos, rigid
rules, and unexamined norms. Those well-
worn "they're just resistant" lines that can
crowd out adaptability.
The film keeps running. The view narrows.
The plot feels...uninspired.
You've seen this film before.
What we think or feel starts to stand in for
what is.
How we act stands in for what is needed.
And the scene plays again...and again.
This is the cinema inside our heads.
This is hooked.

Gentle Acceptance
One of the great paradoxes of human experience is that we
can't change ourselves, our circumstances, or our workplaces,
nor can we effectively lead others, until we see and accept
what exists right now, Acceptance is a prerequisite for change,
When we allow the world to be as it is, we free ourselves to
move on,
Acceptance is not passive resignation or agreement, It isn't
liking the thing, Rather, acceptance is contact with what is
in service of what matters,
Gentle Acceptance is noticing, with kindness: this is here,

@ WATCH

not your feelings, When you say, "I am sad," your
identity becomes fused with the emotion, You become
this gray cloud of sadness, Instead, when you say, "I
notice that I'm feeling sad," you create space between
yourself and the emotion, You become the sky, and the
gray cloud of sadness is simply passing through, You are
not the cloud, You are the whole damn sky!

Shadow Avoidance
Avoidance keeps us from facing what's real, It stalls growth, dulls
adaptability, undermines well-being, and blocks the conversations
that bring teams, relationships, and cultures alive, We avoid
what's uncomfortable — emotion, conflict, uncertainty — and
trade truth for brief relief,
Three shadow forms of avoidance:
o Brooding: circling the story until we are trapped inside it,
o Bottling: pushing feelings down until they push back,
o Forced Positivity: papering over emotion and nuance with
hollow cheer,

Widening the frame

Astronauts describe the ' 'overview effect," the jolt Of
seeing Earth as a small blue marble.
From that distance, what once felt absolute finds its
place in a larger scene. Our view is one view, not the
whole. Without that perspective, we jump to
conclusions, make unwise decisions, and act in ways
that do not serve us.
Stepping Out builds that perspective. It's at the heart
of well-being. It steadies hard conversations, helps
groups move through conflict, and frees whole
systems to break old patterns.
When we are stuck, a story is authoring us. When we
create space, we agency.
This is stepping out.

across an ocean. Lasting change works the same way, in a life, a

connection. Emotional Agility helps us move from "l have to fix
